rv.q: “The Other Josh Cohen” is a charmer, touching on real issues without pummeling them.
With its cartoonish brand of comedy and zippy performances from the cast, The Other Josh Cohen is the deliriously fun musical we all need right now.
The show is fun, lively and kept a smile on my face the whole time.
It’s a simple life-affirming message delivered in a silly, joyful package.

There’s a reason this zingy little musical has gone from downtown’s Soho Playhouse to New Jersey’s Paper Mill Playhouse to Rochester’s Geva Theatre Center to, now, finally, off-Broadway’s cozy Westside Theatre.
The Other Josh Cohen is a light and lively diversion that’s probably going to keep a smile on your face for its 95-minute entirety.
With a fun score that sometimes riffs off of Josh's beloved Neil Diamond and a clever book that's heavy on urban Jewish humor and pop culture references
The Other Josh Cohen succeeds with a humble and open-hearted modesty.
Anyone looking for an undemanding hour and a half of Seinfeldian shtick, even if some of it has crept by its sell-by date, will probably get his or her money's worth.
Mildly entertaining...Yet somehow, the humor in 'The Other Josh Cohen' often feels cliché and dated.
This is one fabulously funny feel-good show that shouldn’t be missed, and another triumph for Off-Broadway, in a season of stellar offerings.
Fortunately for theatergoers, Josh Cohen is in and of itself the payoff at the end of the line, the best show audiences will have seen in years.
Foster manages to stage this musical with an economy that boggles the imagination, and he makes these characters transcend time, place, and space with shimmering brilliance.
Like the pints of ice cream that year-ago Josh gobbles down, this confection, er, I mean production, proves impossible to resist.

"A sweet and winning musical comedy...'The Other Josh Cohen' bounces from song to song with high energy and infectious humor. The very able cast plays multiple roles as well as their own instruments, and the costume and wig designers do great work.
That said, “The Other Josh Cohen” continues to entertain and celebrate hope in uncertain and challenging times.
Ultimately, The Other Josh Cohen is a worthy musical because it is so optimistic.

cn.t: Critics embrace this charming Off-Broadway musical as a delightful, laugh-out-loud rom-com with tremendous heart. Rosen and Rossmer's witty dual performance, clever pop culture humor, and uplifting message about resilience resonate in a brisk, irresistible 90 minutes.
